report.source_text: A following CT-angio with i.v. contrast infusion in arterial and venous phases was performed, revealing a giant splenic aneurysm 9.8 cm in diameter and 5 cm in length, located in the previous common ligation of the splenic vessels (Figures 1–3). clinician.trajectory_summary: A 43-year-old man presented with fever and ascites. Initial CT scan revealed a large amount of free ascites and a giant mass in the left upper abdomen near the pancreas and paraaortic area (E001). Subsequent CT angiography confirmed a giant splenic aneurysm measuring 9.8 cm with a concomitant arteriovenous shunt via the enlarged splenic vein at the site of prior splenectomy (E002). Six days later, the patient developed fever recurrence, paralytic ileus, low hematocrit, and elevated inflammatory markers (referenced but quantitative lab values not documented), with imaging showing hemorrhagic pancreatitis and minor bleeding near the stomach atrium (E007). Three days postoperative, portal vein thrombosis occurred, leading to modification of anticoagulant therapy (E006). Approximately 24 hours after admission, he underwent open repair surgery which revealed a fragile hemorrhagic lesion with covered rupture encased in a giant omental sac and 4 liters of ascites with blood in the peritoneal cavity, supporting peritoneal infection and portal hypertension (E004, E008).

key_supporting_evidence.claim: CT scan revealed free ascites and a giant mass in the left upper abdomen near pancreas and paraaortic area on admission.
CT angiography showed a 9.8 cm giant splenic aneurysm and concomitant arteriovenous shunt via the splenic vein at the prior splenectomy site.
Six days later, fever recurrence with paralytic ileus, low hematocrit, and imaging showed hemorrhagic pancreatitis and minor bleeding near stomach atrium.
Postoperative portal vein thrombosis was diagnosed; anticoagulation therapy was adjusted.
Open laparotomy revealed fragile hemorrhagic aneurysm rupture within omental sac, 4 liters of ascites and blood in peritoneal cavity, confirming infection and portal hypertension features.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Imaging and surgery showed no major bleeding, only minor bleeding in the stomach region (E007)
